# Rockstar workers vote 75-25 against IWGB union recognition
Rockstar Games employees voted 75-25 against IWGB recognition, with 1,544 ballots cast across 93% turnout. The union pledges continued organizing amid an active employment tribunal.

Rockstar Games employees have voted 75% against a union recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union, closing a two-week ballot that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.
The IWGB confirmed the split: 25% of Rockstar workers backed the recognition deal, 75% rejected it. Turnout was remarkably high for a workplace vote. The IWGB said the result does not stop employees from organizing or exercising union rights. What Rockstar loses — or avoids, depending on your read — is any obligation to regularly meet union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters. The company negotiated no recognition deal, and now it doesn't have to.
The IWGB framed the loss as a starting point rather than a verdict. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union said in a statement. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues."
